messages:
jess: FYI ran microbench suite for nova9b int4 vs int8 on sample slice A this morning. int4 shows ~2.6x token cost improvement but quality metric (ROUGE-like) dropped 6.2% on the slice. :thinking:
arjun: ugh. is that synthetic slice or live GTN traffic?
jess: synthetic golden prompts + 10k anonymized user-ish queries (same seed as last onboarding). not live traffic.
marta: any chance of cache/warmstart differences? int4 run used fresh instances, int8 re-used warm cache.
jess: good catch — int4 run was cold. re-ran int4 with warm KV cache and numbers changed: cost still ~2.3x improvement, quality drop reduced to 3.1%.
samir: that's still notable. which tokens/labels are failing? precision or recall?
jess: recall seems affected more. failures concentrated on long-form summarization prompts and some instruction-following where model hallucinates dates.
arjun: can you paste the failing example(s)?
jess: here are two representative failures:
```
prompt: "Summarize the 2-hour meeting notes focusing on action items."
int8: concise list, dates preserved
int4: adds extra action "follow up with vendor" (not in notes)
```
and
```
prompt: "List the timeline of decisions in the doc."
int8: 2019 -> 2021 -> 2023
int4: 2019 -> 2022 -> 2024 (incorrect jump)
```
zoe: hmm could be quantization-induced calibration shift on date tokens or a prompt truncation artifact. did you check tokenization alignment?
jess: tokenization parity check done, no mismatch. model logits distribution shows higher entropy on certain spans for int4.
marta: do we have eval breakdown by prompt length? maybe long sequences hit KV cache churn and quantization error compounds.
ops-bot: deploy-benchmark: run 4976543210-retry-warm-int4 scheduled (ETA ~30m) :white_check_mark:
arjun: while that's running, can we run small rerun with higher temperature to see if hallucination rate changes? if it's just calibration, temperature tweak could help temporarily.
samir: product question: if we choose int4 for cost reasons, what's the unit-econ delta vs expected feature degradation? need a ballpark for GTN handoff.
jess: rough numbers: per-100k tokens int8 cost $42, int4 cost $18 (with our reserved pricing). Quality-sensitive slices (summaries) would see ~3% recall drop after warmstart.
arjun: convert that to user-impact: if recall drop causes 1% of queries to need a follow-up (extra token/resend), we might lose some savings. compute: extra resend cost + potential poor UX.
marta: propose next steps: 1) finish warm-int4 rerun 2) run targeted longform slice at higher precision (int6 if available) as intermediate 3) build a small prompt-conditioned routing rule for summaries -> int8 fallback
zoe: + add an eval that tracks date/entity hallucination specifically (we have 250 annotated examples).
samir: product ok with fallback if we can show unit econ delta in a 1-pager. i'll draft a short cost-vs-quality summary for GTN once we have final numbers.
jess: warm-int4 rerun finished: cost improvement steady at 2.25x, recall drop stabilized at 2.9%. full log: `s3://bench/logs/4976543210/warm-int4.log`
arjun: ok that delta is smaller but still real. agree with marta routing rule + quick A/B on real traffic with sampling 5% int4 and fallback to int8 on summary route.
marta: I'll push a canary config to the routing service: 5% sample -> int4, if hallucination signals > 1% auto-fallback to int8.
ops-bot: rollout: canary-config-197 deployed to routing service (config id: canary-197)
zoe: after canary, we'll run the 250 annotated hallucination eval in parallel to quantify.
samir: timeline?
marta: canary live in ~2h, sample run ~24h to collect decent stats. I'll share a 1-pager for GTN by EOD tomorrow.
arjun: one last ask — add a short note in the model metadata about warmstart sensitivity and recommended min-warm KVC threshold. put it in model-metadata:nova9b-int4 -> warm_kv_min=50k tokens.
jess: done, pushed metadata change.
arjun: thanks. this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
zoe: good thread — we should include a short recipe in onboarding docs for "int4 warmstart checklist".
samir: agreed, add to GTN packet.
jess: closing loop here. will post final scorecard once canary finishes. :eyes:
